speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing this double vision and muscle weakness, and did it come on suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually occurs when I look up or down, but not when I look straight ahead. The weakness in my arms and legs feels worse after climbing stairs or doing other activities, but it gets better if I rest for a while. I have not noticed any changes in balance or coordination, and I do not have tingling or numbness, just the weakness and fatigue.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of thyroid problems, and have you noticed any swelling or tenderness in your neck? Also, has your double vision been present since the beginning or did it develop later?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not noticed any issues with eye tracking or movement when looking straight ahead. I have not had any recent infections or fevers, and I do not have a family history of neurological disorders. The weakness feels symmetrical, affecting both arms and both legs equally.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any difficulty swallowing, chewing, or speaking, especially towards the end of the day? Also, have you noticed any changes in your facial muscles, such as a drooping smile or difficulty keeping your eyes fully open?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had any trouble swallowing or slurred speech, and I have not noticed any breathing problems or shortness of breath. I have not had any recent trauma to my neck or head, and I do not have any known allergies. The symptoms started gradually about a month ago and get worse with activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Test. Do you have any droopy eyelids that get worse as the day goes on, or does your smile look asymmetric after smiling for a while?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated). Additional findings include ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze, diminished motor strength in upper extremities, and decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation on electromyography. Chest CT is normal with no thymoma detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated antibodies and your specific symptoms confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
